Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 marked a period of significant advancement for Apex EV, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included our gross margin expansion to 19.2%, up 320 basis points quarter-over-quarter, driven by Fremont Gigafactory hitting 95% utilization and declining battery costs; record production of 285,000 vehicles, up 42% year-over-year, with strong capacity utilization averaging 82% globally; ASP trends showing a blended $58,200, up 4.2% year-over-year, with premium SUVs leading the way; effective raw material cost management yielding a 22% reduction per vehicle through hedging and diversification; sustained gross margin trends building to 19.8% consolidated; notable electric vehicle range improvements averaging 18% uplift to 420 miles on our Apex S; and robust revenue outlook with Q4 guidance at $2.6 to $2.9 billion. The launch of our Apex X SUV has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image through higher customer satisfaction and market share gains.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue was $2.5 billion, representing a substantial 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 19.2%, driven by increased production efficiencies and favorable product mix. Operating expenses totaled $450 million, and net income amounted to $150 million. We are in a strong financial position with $3.2 billion in cash reserves. We project $2.8 billion to $3.0 billion for Q4.

As we turn to our gross margin outlook, we delivered a company gross margin of 19.2% in Q3, up 320 basis points quarter-over-quarter and marking our sixth consecutive quarter of margin expansion. This was driven by our Fremont Gigafactory hitting 95% utilization rates on the Apex S sedan line, combined with a 12% sequential decline in battery cell costs per kWh, thanks to our ramp on in-house 4680 cylindrical cells—now representing 65% of our pack content, up from 40% a year ago.

Our consolidated gross margin expanded to 19.8%, up 210 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 17.7% in Q1 and 340 basis points year-over-year from 16.4% in Q2 2023. This marks our strongest quarterly gross margin since Q4 2022, driven by a combination of manufacturing efficiencies, favorable product mix, and strategic cost-outs that are positioning us ahead of peers. Automotive gross margin hit 18.5% – a 280 bps QoQ improvement and 410 bps YoY gain. Excluding regulatory credits, which contributed $120 million or about 1.2 points to the margin, our adjusted automotive margin was a robust 17.3%. This outperforms recent industry benchmarks and reflects our relentless focus on cost per vehicle.

Key drivers included economies of scale with 28,500 vehicles delivered, up 45% YoY, fixed cost absorption improving by 3.2 points as utilization exceeded 85%; battery cost reductions of 22% YoY through in-house 4680 production at 50 GWh annual capacity and LFP shifts, bringing pack costs to $105/kWh; favorable mix with ASP at $52,400, up $2,100 QoQ, and software attach rates at 42%; plus headwinds navigated like raw material volatility offset by 70% hedging. Regionally, North America led at 21.2% with IRA credits averaging $9,200; Europe at 14.8% amid subsidy phase-outs; China at 12.5% prioritizing profitability. Energy and services hit 28.4% on $250 million revenue. Trailing four quarters trended up from 15.2% to 18.9%, on track for 22%+ by year-end.

Looking ahead, we're guiding for a full-year 2024 company gross margin of 21% to 23%, with automotive gross margins specifically at 20% to 22%. For Q4, we expect automotive gross margins to land at 22% to 24%, reflecting continued cost discipline and a richer product mix. Volume forecasts Q4 deliveries at 28,000 to 32,000 units, a 25% sequential increase from Apex S refresh and Apex X shipments; ASP at $52,000 to $54,000 with higher-margin trims and IRA credits; COGS per unit $38,000 to $40,000, down 8%, led by LFP at $55/kWh and 4680 dry electrode; North America 70% mix at 24% margins; regulatory credits $150 million; FX and commodities stable. In 2025, margins to 25%+ with Apex X scale and energy storage at 45%. Q3 guidance was 20.2-20.8%, with next-gen platform, vertical integration, and supply resilience.

On average selling price trends, our global blended ASP came in at $58,200, up 4.2% year-over-year and 1.8% quarter-over-quarter, marking the third consecutive quarter of sequential growth, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin SUV and pickup platforms. By model, Apex S sedan at $49,800 ASP, up 2.1% YoY, with Long Range AWD and Autonomy Pro upgrades; Vanguard SUV equivalent Apex X at $62,400, up 6.8% YoY on Performance trims; Titan Pickup at $82,500, up 7.5% YoY; BoltMax compact at $32,100. Regionally, North America $64,300 (52% volume), up 8.1% with IRA $6,200; Europe $54,200 (22%), down 1.2%; China $41,800 (18%), down 5.4% YoY; Rest of World $56,700. Targeting $62k blended by YE '25 via mix optimization, services, and cost-downs.

For Q4 2024, we guide revenue to $2.6 billion to $2.9 billion, 28% to 38% YoY growth, on 32,000 to 36,000 deliveries; vehicle revenue $2.3B-$2.5B at $72,000 ASP; energy/services $250M-$350M; credits $50M-$100M. Full-year 2025 $13.0B-$15.0B, 45-65% growth, 160k-185k deliveries; vehicles $11.5B-$13.0B at $68k-$70k ASP; energy $1.2B-$1.5B; credits $300M-$500M. Tailwinds: battery to $80/kWh, SiC integration, software at 20% attach; risks like rates and price wars mitigated by margins.

Next, Maria Gonzalez will share updates on our manufacturing operations.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, Jordan. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency. Our efforts have resulted in record production volumes and reduced manufacturing costs.

Today, I'd like to dive into our production volume and capacity utilization rates, which remain the cornerstone of our operational excellence at Apex EV. In the EV sector, these metrics are critical leading indicators of our ability to scale amid surging demand. In Q3 2024, we achieved record production of 285,000 vehicles, a 42% year-over-year increase from 200,000 units in Q3 2023, and a 12% sequential ramp from Q2's 254,000. This was driven by our Apex X crossover platform at 62% of output or 177,000 units, with Apex S sedan and Apex Pro pickup at 68,000 and 40,000 units.

Capacity utilization averaged 82% globally across 1.2 million annual run-rate, up from 71% YoY. North America (Fremont and Spartanburg) at 91% on 400k capacity, producing 92,000; Europe (Berlin) at 76% on 300k, 57,000 units; China (Shanghai JV) at 74% on 500k, 136,000 units. North America powerhouse at 91% with IRA; Europe lagging on demand but rebounding; China growth engine targeting 90% year-end. Trends: YoY growth outpaced deliveries by 2%, inventory 18 days. Initiatives: advanced robotics/digital twins slashing defects to 0.8/1k; battery gigapress at 45s cycles; supply resilience with 80% localized semis.

Accelerating to 1.8M capacity by 2026 with $2.5B capex: Reno 4680 gigafactory, Spartanburg Phase 2. Guide Q4 310k-320k units at 85-88% utilization. Risks like lithium up 10% QoQ buffered by 60% fixed contracts.

After me, we will hear from Dr. Elena Vasquez regarding our technological advancements.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Maria. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. We are committed to developing cutting-edge solutions that will shape the future of mobility.

Before questions, I'd like to highlight our standout achievements in electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains, foundational to our leadership and contributing to 28% YoY delivery growth and 15% margin expansion. Across Apex S sedan and Apex X SUV, average EPA range uplifted 18% YoY: Apex S to 420 miles on 102 kWh pack from 355; Apex X to 380 from 320. Efficiency to 215 Wh/mi from 248, or 13% gain, WLTP 18.5 kWh/100km.

From multi-pronged roadmap: battery with 4680 silicon anodes at 850 Wh/L, 280 Wh/kg pack-level, $85/kWh; 800V architectures at 95% adoption, 30% faster charging, 12% inverter losses cut via SiC, 75% regen; thermal mgmt 98% efficiency at -10°C. Aerodynamics Cd 0.198, mass down 8% to 1,950 kg via gigacastings/structural packs.

Regionally: NA NPS +22 to 92/100, 35% growth; Europe outpacing VW ID.7, 12% share; China 150k units. Drives $450 lifetime value per 10 Wh/mi gain, 72% resale. OTA +5% fleet-wide; 2025 solid-state for 500 miles, $2.2B capex. These are financial accelerants for raised FY24 guidance.

Following me, Raj Patel will provide insights into our supply chain management.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Elena. We have implemented robust supply chain strategies to mitigate risks and ensure the reliable flow of materials. Our focus on diversification and strategic partnerships has strengthened our supply chain resilience.

As we discuss Q3 results, raw material sourcing and cost management is a critical lever, with battery metals and structurals at 42% COGS. We delivered 22% YoY reduction in raw material costs per vehicle, saving $1,450 on Apex S equivalent, contributing to 28.7% margins.

Battery raws: lithium to $14,500/ton from $82k peak; nickel $16k/ton down 35%; cobalt $18.5k. Strategies: 65% lithium offtake at $22k/ton with Albemarle/SQM; nickel JV Tsingshan 40k tons at $15.2k; NA diversification to 45% LFP via Livent for IRA; Europe recycled via Redwood. Vehicle: secondary aluminum 55% at $1,950 equiv; steel $850/ton.

Technical: LFP 62% output, $62/kWh cathode; sodium-ion pilots $50/kWh; Li-Cycle 12 GWh recycling $85M credits. Inventory 90 days AI-optimized, 70% hedged. Ahead of OEMs, expect 8-10% decline FY24. Multi-modal logistics mitigates disruptions. Turned headwind to 450 bps tailwind, sub-$100/kWh by 2025.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Sarah for the Q&A session.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1 (Morgan Stanley):
Thanks for the update. Alex, at a high level, how do you see the competitive landscape evolving with new entrants, and what's Apex EV's moat?

Alex Rivera:
Great question. Our moat is vertical integration from cells to software, as evidenced by 4680 ramp and ApexOS autonomy. With global EV TAM to 20M by 2027, we're positioned for 2-3% U.S. share via premium volume, fleet deals, and efficiency edges that peers lack. Disciplined pricing avoids China wars, focusing on IRA-fueled NA dominance.

Analyst 2 (Goldman Sachs):
Jordan, can you expand on the ASP assumptions in your Q4 guidance and potential pricing pressures?

Jordan Lee:
Absolutely. Q4 ASP $52k-$54k assumes 55% long-range AWD and 20% Apex X at $68k, no U.S. cuts with 9.5% EV share stabilizing. Europe incentives offset OEM pressure; China limited exposure. Blended $58.2k this quarter shows premiumization—SUVs at $62.4k, pickups $82.5k—targeting $62k YE '25 via 45% SUV/pickup mix and 28% autonomy attach.

Analyst 3 (JPMorgan):
Maria, with production at 285k, what's the ramp plan for Q4 utilization and any bottlenecks?

Maria Gonzalez:
Solid progress to 85-88% Q4 on 310k-320k guide. Fremont 98%+, Reno Phase 2 at 70% for Apex X packs. No major bottlenecks—AI scheduling, cobots, gigapress unlocked 15% throughput. Capex accelerates to 1.8M run-rate, hedging lithium volatility.

Analyst 4 (Barclays):
Elena, impressive range gains—how do these translate to customer adoption and future R&D spend?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Range to 420 miles and 215 Wh/mi drove NPS to 92, 35% NA growth, 20% TCO edge for fleets. OTA neural nets add continuous gains; 2025 solid-state Samsung JV for 500 miles. R&D at $2.2B scales production 25% YoY, monetizing via higher resale 72% at 36 months.

Analyst 5 (Citi):
Raj, on raw materials, with lithium correction, how hedged are you for reflation risks?

Raj Patel:
Well-hedged: 65% lithium at $22k/ton through 2026, 60% fixed contracts. LFP 62% eliminates Ni/Co; recycling 92% yield at 60% virgin cost. NA/EU localization de-risks; expect 8-10% further decline FY24 despite Red Sea +5% freight.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Analyst 6 (Piper Sandler):
Alex, overall, does the guidance bake in macro softening, and what's the free cash flow path?

Alex Rivera:
Guidance embeds resilience—40% fleet backlog offsets consumer sentiment; 18% FY25 margins give pricing power. First positive FCF this year, scaling to sustainable profitability on gigafactory expansions and software ramps. Well-positioned for EV demand growth.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
